[agentorg](https://github.com/georgedouzas/agentorg) is a framework for generating multi-agent organisations from one Python file,
`spec.py`. It's still early and isn't on PyPI yet, so install it from GitHub:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/georgedouzas/agentorg.git
agentorg --help
```

```
Usage: agentorg [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Agentorg: Generate runnable multi-agent organisations.

Options:
  --version  Show the version and exit.
  --help     Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  new     Interview the user to assemble an agentorg spec.py.
  render  Render a project from a specification file.
  ui      Run the browser-based master interview UI.
```

`agentorg new` starts an interview with a master agent, which fills in the spec for you. There is also `agentorg ui` if you prefer a
browser. The interview moves through five stages: discover, configure, build, refine and handoff. Each stage's agent only has the
tools for that stage, so the discovery agent can't set your organisation's identity by accident.

`agentorg render` then turns the spec into a project. By default that's the full thing, with a backend and a React dashboard. You
can also render just the frontend, backend or AI layer.

The master agent uses [Agno](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno), but your own agents, teams and workflows don't have to. In the spec,
each one can be anything runnable, like a plain async function.
